Future host is `C:/Users/Victor Colosi/dev/Fabel 5 Trace 3D`; DO NOT modify that repo in v1. Astra owns scope and review; Terra is the coding delegate. This is standalone implementation work, not a bug report against the Hedral MEP production platform.

Read `docs/hydronics/implementation-plan.md` and `docs/hydronics/discovery-and-decisions.md` in PRD maker. Local read-only audit/evidence reports are in `.pi/research/hydronics-*.md`. Workbook source: `C:/Users/Victor Colosi/Desktop/Home Page/Mechanical/Calculations- One Note/SHG_Pump PD Calc.xlsm`. Do not execute its macros, alter or upload the workbook, copy client metadata, or ship whole source PDFs.

Approved scope: closed filled loops at prescribed terminal design GPM, shared physical supply/return sections, complete circuits, named-source water and 30/40/50 volume-percent-glycol PG/EG, one mean temperature per system, water 32–200°F/glycol 30–200°F, selected pipe sizes, small verified fitting library plus manual losses. Results in feet of actual fluid and loss-equivalent psi (pressure equivalent of required pump total head, not unconditional flange static gauge differential). Correct spreadsheet defects, use laminar math, block transitional-flow final recommendations, and require explicit margin acknowledgment with no preset. No drawing tools, nonlinear flow balancing, open-system static lift, NPSH, pump curves, automatic sizing or compliance claim.

Implementation belongs in self-contained `hydronics/`, with a pure TypeScript engine independent of React/browser/Fabel and one versioned `hydronic-pressure-drop@1` JSON contract. Preserve unrelated files and dependencies. No commit, push, deployment or Fabel changes without separate approval. Build/typecheck before tests; independent review required before Done.

tickets.title: Hydronic PD v1 — qualify reference data and define the portable contract
tickets.body:
## Outcome
Establish a versioned, unit-explicit calculation boundary and verified data that later math/UI can use without inventing missing engineering values.

## Work
Bootstrap the isolated TypeScript project/tooling without replacing PRD-maker tooling. Define stable IDs, pump boundaries, directed supply/terminal/return sections, ordered circuit references, prescribed terminal GPM, discriminated loss elements, fluid reference, margin/acknowledgment, validation/completeness and provenance contracts. Provide the pure engine barrel.

Implement IAPWS SR6-08(2011) water density eq.(2) and viscosity eq.(7). Verify/pin the needed dense DOWFROST and DOWTHERM SR-1 guide columns for 30/40/50 volume percent glycol, not percent commercial concentrate. Visually verify source pages/cells and record URLs, document revision/hash, page/table/unit and conversion. Do not blend incompatible revisions or silently correct suspicious cells. Proposed interpolation is adjacent-node linear density/log-linear viscosity with quantified checks; stop for material discrepancies. Range checks must prohibit extrapolation, unknown fluids, missing cells and water fallback. Label typical product-reference approximation and single-phase assumption.

Create a bounded source-verified pipe-ID catalog (target common 1/2–12 inch steel Sch 10/40/80 and copper K/L/M; unsupported combinations explicit), actual-ID/roughness override, and a small traceable fitting catalog plus manual K/EL. At the source checkpoint Victor explicitly chose generic DOE-HDBK-1012/3-92 standard90/45 elbow Le/D estimates (30/16), with current-basis engineer confirmation, turbulent-only preset guard and honest unspecified manufacturer/connection metadata. This is not universal glycol/laminar qualification; do not substitute copper Hazen–Williams EL. Keep ratios tied to current actual diameter rather than stale fixed equivalent feet. Qualify literal dimensional designations at EVERY size: 12-inch STD versus Sch 40 and 10/12-inch XS versus Sch 80 differ inside this range. Do not substitute STD/XS/S-suffix entries under literal schedule labels. Cross-check ID=OD-2*wall and independent dimensions; inconsistent sources require disposition. Coefficients must state applicable connection geometry/size/regime/fluid basis. Reducers outside verified presets use explicit manual K. No water-only EL table claimed universally valid for glycol.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Engine contract has explicit IP units and stable schema version; no React/DOM/store dependency.
- [ ] Official IAPWS verification at 298.15 K recovers rho 997.047013 kg/m³ and mu 889.996774 microPa·s within published numeric precision.
- [ ] Every shipped glycol node has traceable rendered-source verification; exact-node and units tests pass. Concentration/product labels and software ranges are explicit.
- [ ] Interpolation checks and actual errors are recorded; ambiguous/unverified data never masquerades as working support.
- [ ] Unsupported pipe/fitting/range/unknown-fluid input produces structured errors, never fabricated zero or water substitution.
- [ ] Independent data review can reproduce transcription and conversions from provenance notes.

## Validation / handoff
Run strict build/typecheck and dataset/contract tests. Return qualified source manifest, unresolved data decisions, changed files and commands. SOURCE CHECKPOINT UPDATE: Victor approved pinned DOWFROST September 2001 and DOWTHERM SR-1 February 2008 English tables with dated typical-property labels/no revision splicing. Astra independently found shifted EG density columns and set per-series LOO max regression limits: density<=0.025%, viscosity<=1.5%, Re<=1.5%, representative head<=0.5%, plus independent exact source nodes. See docs/hydronics/foundation-parent-review.md for rationale, source/cell evidence and conflict dispositions. These are table regression checks, not product-accuracy guarantees. Repair and revalidation are mandatory before HYD-001 Done or dependent implementation. Deliver provisional data/qualification harnesses for review, never advertise them as qualified. This ticket blocks dependent work if a promised option cannot be qualified; report that rather than silently narrowing scope.

tickets.title: Hydronic PD v1 — implement validated pipe, fitting, valve and equipment losses
tickets.body:
## Outcome
One pure calculation path returns auditable hydraulic losses with explicit invalid/incomplete states and correct actual-fluid head/pressure semantics.

## Work
Implement actual-ID geometry, GPM velocity, dynamic-viscosity Reynolds number, Darcy friction and typed PIPE/K/EL/Cv/actual-psi/actual-fluid-feet elements. Use Darcy not Fanning factor. Re<2000 uses 64/Re; 2000<=Re<=4000 blocks final recommendations; Re>4000 uses bounded/residual-checked Colebrook. Zero-flow low-level functions avoid division by zero; active design demand validation belongs to the circuit layer.

Use h=f(L/D)v²/(2g), K loss nKv²/(2g), EL n f(EL/D)v²/(2g), and density-aware psi/head conversion. Cv uses SG relative to explicitly documented 60°F reference water: psi=SG(Q/Cv)². Actual-fluid-head conversion cancels operating density; do not multiply SG twice. Require applicable manufacturer turbulent/nonchoked Cv confirmation; no universal viscous correction and no inference from pipe Re. Unqualified manufacturer pressure basis or K/EL applicability must stay visible and block final design acceptance where unresolved. Bind confirmation to current derived section GPM, fluid/reference/concentration/temperature, relevant geometry, element type/data and declared envelope; invalidate after indirect shared-flow changes too. Require requalification outside that basis, including on import. Never auto-scale one-point psi/head with Q². Store K/EL velocity/diameter basis; omit a preset whose other-leg/split basis cannot be represented.

Preserve categories separately from formula: valve K/EL is still valve for margin. Model relevant fields per element type; missing/irrelevant stale fields cannot silently contribute. Count quantities are nonnegative integers, Cv positive, lengths/K/direct losses finite nonnegative, actual ID/density/viscosity positive. Known K=0 differs from unknown K.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All element modes have independent hand-check fixtures and explainable itemized output.
- [ ] Laminar Poiseuille, turbulent residual, exact regime boundaries, zero flow, nonconvergence and invalid-number tests pass.
- [ ] Actual-fluid psi/head round trips and standard Cv SG cancellation are tested for water and glycol densities.
- [ ] Legacy water-row arithmetic is separately reproduced with declared legacy properties; changes from precise constants/named-source properties are documented rather than hidden.
- [ ] Transitional/unqualified calculations are not returned as final design-ready losses.
- [ ] Nominal-vs-actual ID and missing-FEET-branch legacy defects have recurrence tests.
- [ ] UI needs no second hydraulic formula implementation.

## Validation / handoff
Strict build then tests; report units/constants, residual tolerance, exact fixture expectations and comparison notes. Use `Calc Ex (E.L.)!row13` only as a declared-property arithmetic fixture, not certification of fluid data.

tickets.title: Hydronic PD v1 — evaluate shared supply/return circuits and governing pump head
tickets.body:
## Outcome
Evaluate the highest-loss complete closed circuit at specified terminal flows without double-counting common piping or adding parallel pressure losses.

## Work
Validate stable references/endpoints and ordered discharge→supply→unique terminal→return→suction circuits. Enforce a supply splitting tree and independently routed return merging tree. Reject cycles, unsupported meshes, repeated sections/terminals, broken/reversed connections, mixed supply-return nodes and pump-boundary shortcuts. Direct/reverse return must be represented explicitly, never by doubling supply length.

Derive section GPM from active circuit membership; shared supply and return carry summed terminal demands. Calculate a physical section once and include its identical loss/itemization once in each traversing circuit. Unused stored sections are visibly draft/unassigned. Any invalid/incomplete active circuit blocks the overall pump-head recommendation instead of being omitted.

Return per-circuit/category totals, system flow, raw and margin-adjusted governing paths, deterministic ties and source/completeness evidence. Margin is explicit percentage units: raw=sum(category head), margin=(marginPercent/100)*sum(selected category head), factored=raw+margin. Require finite marginPercent>=0 and a valid deduplicated category set. Apply once; no preset, acknowledgment required even at zero; no active circuits means no acceptance. Test A=10 pipe+20 equipment versus B=20 pipe+9 equipment: 25% pipe-only gives 32.5 versus 34 ft and changes the governing path. Governing design head is maximum AFTER selected margin, not arbitrary selected circuit or sum of parallel losses.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A 10+20 GPM two-terminal fixture has 30 GPM common supply/return and 10/20 GPM individual branches.
- [ ] Every path includes common supply and return exactly once; parallel losses are never summed.
- [ ] Unequal return routing, branch equipment losses, non-longest governing path, ties and margin-changing governing circuit are tested.
- [ ] Row/category/circuit totals reconcile at full calculation precision.
- [ ] Missing active circuit data blocks system acceptance even when another circuit computes successfully.
- [ ] Duplicate/reused/unknown IDs, terminal reuse, discontinuity, reversal, cycles/meshes and invalid GPM produce actionable errors.
- [ ] Building height is never added as static lift in this closed-loop model.

## Validation / handoff
Run strict build then graph/flow/aggregation tests. Supply a small independent hand-calculated circuit fixture and a checkpoint for independent review before UI implementation. No claim of balancing, actual flow distribution or pump operating-point solution.

tickets.title: Hydronic PD v1 — build the section/circuit editor and Show the math interface
tickets.body:
## Outcome
An engineer can author shared piping and complete circuits, see the governing head, and audit the exact calculation in a standalone browser without drawing tools.

## Work
Build a Vite/React TypeScript UI under `hydronics/` with project/system/fluid/mean-temperature controls; section endpoint/role/material/size/actual-ID/roughness/length and loss-element editor; circuit terminal-GPM and ordered supply/terminal/return selection; and result cards/table. Edit shared section data once. Include a synthetic, non-client two-terminal example with shared supply/return and explicit equipment losses.

Show nominal and actual ID, section GPM, velocity, friction rate, regime and actionable validation. Add/duplicate/delete should preserve stable references or demand explicit repair; no invisible dangling deletion. Element switches remove incompatible contribution. Keep text-edit blanks/partial numbers invalid, not coerced to zero. Show a full-circuit Show the math inspector using engine items and cumulative totals, not duplicate formulas. Display source/manual-input provenance and all-active-circuit completeness.

Offer explicit margin selection/acknowledgment and later acceptance only for the complete governing system result. The selected detail path may be non-governing but cannot replace design head. Use localhost 5175, strict port, not Fabel's 5173/8090.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] User can create two circuits sharing supply/return without duplicating physical section records.
- [ ] Shared length/size/flow-demand edits update every affected circuit via the same engine API.
- [ ] UI shows actual-fluid head plus psi, itemized totals, governing ties and raw/margin distinction.
- [ ] Invalid or transitional active circuit visibly blocks final recommendation/acceptance.
- [ ] Manual fitting/Cv/manufacturer-loss assumptions have explicit user confirmation where required.
- [ ] Accessible labeled controls, keyboard editing and readable desktop layout; no graphical pipe authoring or network balancing implied.
- [ ] Real browser smoke test covers authoring, shared edit, missing input, element switch and math reconciliation.

## Validation / handoff
Build before tests. Run component tests and a real browser flow; save screenshots/evidence and exact local launch command. Do not rely solely on source inspection or server-render tests for the UI.

tickets.title: Hydronic PD v1 — save projects, retain reviewed results and export calculations
tickets.body:
## Outcome
Calculations survive local sessions and can be independently reviewed as versioned JSON, printable math and CSV without confusing stale or incomplete values with current design results.

## Work
Implement validated versioned JSON save/open and browser-local autosave/recovery with no network transmission. Reject unsupported versions and malformed/oversized/nonfinite/reference-invalid imports before replacing current work. Recover gracefully from unavailable/quota-exceeded storage. No full workbook import is required.

Accepted snapshot stores the actual normalized inputs (not a hash alone), optional freshness identity, engine/data versions, governing IDs and raw/margin/factored values. Accept only complete system-governing results after margin/applicability acknowledgment. Relevant edits or data-version changes mark the snapshot stale and retain the prior value visibly; view selection/timestamps must not cause numerical staleness. Imported snapshots may display historical values, but require fresh explicit local acceptance; matching recomputation does not authenticate prior human approval. Applicability confirmations separately require matching current operating basis. Invalid pending editor text blocks acceptance and stales old approval even if a last-valid numeric object remains; distinguish unsaved invalid edits from last recoverable autosave, never claim an un-restorable edit was saved.

Print the selected circuit and system design summary with fluid basis, properties/temperature, assumptions, margin, all itemized losses and completeness. CSV preserves units/provisional reasons. Missing values are unavailable/blank, never false zeros. Escape user-controlled report text and defend CSV formula injection.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] JSON round trip preserves IDs, connections, manual inputs, explicit acknowledgments and identical recomputed results.
- [ ] Malformed/unknown-version import preserves current work and displays reasons.
- [ ] Autosave/recovery failures are visible and do not corrupt current calculation.
- [ ] Accept→edit relevant input→stale-retained result and accepted-zero-margin cases pass.
- [ ] Imported or mismatched acceptance cannot show current local approval without fresh explicit acceptance.
- [ ] Shared equipment qualified at 30 GPM becomes unqualified when another terminal changes shared flow to 50 GPM: retain stale old result, block new acceptance, require requalification; cover fluid/temperature and invalid-text variants.
- [ ] Print/CSV contain the same engine totals, units, warnings and source assumptions as screen.
- [ ] Script/HTML strings and spreadsheet-formula user text are exported safely.

## Validation / handoff
Build then tests, including actual browser file round trip, stale snapshot and export checks. No account, cloud storage, deployment or project PDF embedding.

tickets.title: Hydronic PD v1 — independently validate the calculator and document Fabel handoff
tickets.body:
## Outcome
Deliver a locally runnable, reviewed first pass with reproducible validation and an honest account of engineering differences/limits.

## Work
Run the complete acceptance ladder from data transcription/units through independent hydraulic and circuit fixtures to real browser workflow. Preserve numerical fixtures as separate reference evidence rather than deriving expectations by calling the same implementation under test. Add a reviewed legacy-discrepancy register for corrected broken rows/nominal lookup, regime handling, head units, named-source properties, margin choice, fitting limits and deferred sizing/reducer behavior.

Document install/dev/build/test/browser commands, data provenance, discrete concentration semantics, single mean-temperature/liquid-only assumptions, manual Cv/K/EL qualifications, software ranges and unsupported topology. Describe the pure engine entry point, versioned JSON and future Fabel adapter inputs without importing/editing Fabel.

Parent Astra orchestrates fresh independent data/numerical and workflow/security reviewers; the implementer does not self-certify review. Apply accepted fixes serially and rerun affected gates.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fresh install, strict build/typecheck and full automated tests pass with recorded command evidence.
- [ ] Independent reviewers can reproduce water/table nodes, hydraulic formulas and shared-circuit expected numbers.
- [ ] Real-browser author/edit/invalid/accept/stale/save/open/print/CSV flow is exercised and artifacts inspected.
- [ ] Source qualification and serious completeness/numerical/import defects have no unresolved blockers.
- [ ] Documentation clearly distinguishes arithmetic verification from field-certified sizing or actual-network balancing.
- [ ] Fabel and source workbook are unchanged; no credentials/client metadata/full source PDFs committed.
- [ ] Final handoff lists issue IDs, files, tests, launch URL, source/domain limits and any unexecuted checks.

## Validation / handoff
Mark implemented tickets Done only after parent accepts independent review and final evidence. Do not mark the future integration ticket complete. Do not commit, push, deploy or open a PR without new authorization.

tickets.title: Hydronic PD future — integrate the validated engine when Fabel routing is ready
tickets.body:
## Status / explicit non-goal
FUTURE BACKLOG ONLY. Do not implement this ticket as part of the standalone v1. Victor wants Fabel hydronic authoring to catch up to airside first. This issue records the later seam, not permission to modify Fabel today.

## Future outcome
Fabel supplies verified hydronic terminal flow/fluid/temperature, stable source identity and actual connected supply/return sections to the same reviewed pressure-drop engine, presents the governing pump circuit and math, and uses explicit stale-aware engineer acceptance.

## Preconditions
Standalone validation accepted; Fabel has authoritative hydraulic connectivity and measured/declared lengths/pipe IDs/fittings/equipment data. Existing heating-water riser is schematic and cannot be treated as physical pipe geometry. Terminal reheat GPM and plant-rollup GPM have different populations/rounding/basis; reconcile them before import. New work needs a separate approved integration plan and Fabel repository protocol.

## Future acceptance criteria
- [ ] Host adapter supplies the versioned engine contract without forking hydraulic math or using airside CFM/in.w.g. fields as water data.
- [ ] Fabel source identities and rename/delete reconciliation are explicit; missing data blocks final results, not water/zero fallback.
- [ ] Complete supply/return circuits and common equipment are represented from authoritative inputs, never inferred from schematic SVG length.
- [ ] All active pump circuits determine the maximum; selecting a lower-loss detail path cannot set design head.
- [ ] Host follows sanctioned state/command/undo/save boundaries and retains stale accepted results visibly.
- [ ] Fabel build THEN tests and integration/browser validation pass under its then-current protocol.

## Dependencies
HYD-006 plus future Fabel hydronic-connectivity readiness and Victor's explicit approval. No estimate or promise that the current host can populate the contract automatically.
